title: Echopoint gate held a deploy on a reset of the CLI's own ephemeral claim
summary: At 02:51-02:53Z five connections from the gate runner to the Cloudflare edge reset during the echopoint gate for echopoint#879. Four failures read `Could not connect to …` and were transport by the gate's rule. The fifth was the CLI's own call `claim ephemeral Job: Post …/claim: … connection reset by peer`, which the regex did not list, so the gate reran nothing and held prod. The dispatch for echopoint#880, 45 s later, carried #879 too and promoted it at 02:57Z, so prod waited 3.5 min. The gate's leak report also never ran, because it sits after the verdict, and a throwaway org from a reset cleanup stayed until the routine deleted it at 06:2xZ. This is the third time the transport rule missed a new wording (2026-11-05 runner nodes, 2026-11-13 SSE, now the CLI claim).

impact.text: No customer impact. Prod echopoint promotion of echopoint#879 skipped by one gate; the next dispatch promoted the same code 3.5 min later. One throwaway Anchor org on dev left unreported for about 3.5 h.

trigger: At 02:51:44Z the CLI's claim of an ephemeral execution for `Admin impersonation refusals` (fc768d01) got `connection reset by peer` from 172.64.80.1; at 02:53:19Z the rerun step classified it as a product failure and failed the gate.
detection: The deploy-failure alert ran at 02:53:21Z, overnight. grafana-watch saw the red gate at its next run but filed it on the suite reset row as "same trigger". The routine found the misclassification at its 2026-11-19T06:08Z run while reading the gate log line by line.
resolution: The gate's regex now counts `connection reset by peer` and TCP `i/o timeout` as transport wherever they appear, with samples for the claim and launch calls, and reports leaks of transport-failed flows before its verdict. The routine's run_suites.sh uses the same rule, reruns CLI control-plane failures (claim, complete) like launch failures, and prints `GATE-TRANSPORT-MISSED` for any gate that refused a flow its own rule calls transport.

whys.problem: The echopoint gate for echopoint#879 went red on TCP resets and skipped the prod promotion

because.text: The rerun step called the `Admin impersonation refusals` failure a product failure, so it reran none of the five reset flows
because.evidence: Gate log: `##[error]Flows failed on more than a transport error: fc768d01-ba1c-4bac-8178-41ca2ba144a7.` (job 135302299274)

because.text: The failure was the CLI's own claim call (`claim ephemeral Job: … reset by peer`); the regex knew resets only from runner nodes and SSE
because.evidence: `transport='Could not connect to|Connection refused by|TLS handshake|Could not resolve host|Request to [^ ]+ timed out|SSE stream read error: .*connection reset by peer'` in echopoint-test.yml at 4723f2a

because.text: Each earlier fix added the one wording that had just failed a gate (runner node on 2026-11-05, SSE on 2026-11-13)
because.evidence: ci-workflows#42 and #51 each add one alternative; the 2026-11-13 postmortem action reads `Add the SSE reset class to the gate regex`

because.text: The transport rule lists wordings per caller, not the condition (a reset, an i/o timeout), so each new network caller misses once
The sample self-test proves known wordings still match; it cannot reveal a caller nobody has listed
because.evidence: SAMPLES held 7 messages, all from runner nodes and SSE; none from the CLI's launch, claim or complete calls

because.text: Samples come only from failures already seen, not from the list of calls the CLI makes to the control plane during a gate
Five connections from the gate runner to the Cloudflare edge reset within 90 s
Resets recur on this path every few days and nobody has captured one at the host to see who sends the RST
because.evidence: Ledger suite transport row: resets on 2026-11-05, -07, -08, -10, -11, -12, -13, -15, -18, -19; human action A7 of the 2026-11-16 postmortem, due 2026-11-27

because.text: Finding the reset needs packet captures on the 1340p runner host, a human task with an owner but no result yet (open since 2026-11-05)
A throwaway org from the reset cleanup went unreported, and the red gate was first filed as a known reset
because.evidence: No `TRANSPORT-LEAK` line in job 135302299274; ledger row 53 note 2026-11-19T02:53Z `same trigger, logged here`

because.text: The gate printed leaks only after the verdict, and exited at the verdict when any failure was not transport
because.evidence: echopoint-test.yml at 4723f2a: `exit 1` on `other` before the `for flow in $failed` leak loop

because.text: The leak report depends on the verdict, so the cases that fail the gate are the cases that hide leaks
Triage matched the reset text to the reset row and did not ask whether the gate's own verdict was right
because.evidence: run_suites.sh gate scan printed only TRANSPORT-LEAK and RERUN-REFUSED lines; no check compared the gate's verdict with the routine's rule

because.text: Nothing compares the gate's transport verdict with the routine's rule, so a misclassified gate looks like an ordinary reset

contributing: The impersonation flow's claim happens before any node runs, so the CLI reports the error itself; runner wordings never cover it.
The deploy-failure alert lands in Discord at night with nobody to read it.

well: The gate's sample self-test and the routine's drift check kept both rules in step for the known wordings.
Reading the gate log line by line, not only the ledger, found the real cause.
wrong: Two earlier postmortems fixed the wording that failed, not the transport condition behind it.
A fix that names one caller left the next caller (the CLI itself) uncovered.
lucky: echopoint#880 merged 2 min after #879, so its dispatch promoted the same code 3.5 min later. Without it, prod would have waited for the next echopoint merge, hours later.
The leaked org was a throwaway with no data; a leaked product user or API key would carry real access.

actions.what: Gate regex matches `connection reset by peer` and TCP `i/o timeout` anywhere, with claim and launch samples
Gate prints TRANSPORT-LEAK for every transport-failed flow before its verdict
run_suites.sh uses the same condition rule, reruns CLI claim/complete failures like launch failures, and prints GATE-TRANSPORT-MISSED when a gate refused a flow its rule calls transport
Skill line: classify transport by condition, never by caller wording
Find why the 1340p → Cloudflare edge path resets connections (same as 2026-11-16 A7)

messaging.internal: Echopoint gate for #879 went red on five TCP resets; one was the CLI's own claim call, a wording the gate's transport rule did not list, so nothing reran and the leak report was skipped. #880's gate promoted the same code 3.5 min later. Gate now classifies resets and i/o timeouts anywhere and reports leaks before its verdict.
